newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares gain ahead FOMC, BUX futures.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares gain ahead FOMC, BUX futures.

text.p: Hungarian share prices closed mostly higher in rising turnover on Tuesday as investors' appetite grew ahead of the FOMC meeting.
"Markets recovered a little bit, although cautiousness still was the main characteristic," said Peter Nagy of Postabank Securities.
The BUX index finished at 5,133.65 points, up 40.38, as spot turnover grew to 2.065 billion forints from this year's lowest daily turnover of 1.16 billion on Monday.
BUX futures firmed for all maturities, by between 103.00 and 152.50 points. June BUX closed at 5,450, up 130.50.
Traders said investors were optimistic about the market's long-term outlook.
"Investors, putting aside Fed and an interest rate rise, are optimistic on the long-term," Nagy said. "Many of them think that it was perhaps time to buy, whether there will be a rate hike or not."
Analysts said investors were waiting for a clear trend before fresh investments.

"They're waiting to see whether there will be or not a really decisive correction or whether there will be or not the next trend will be up, because they all still have money they want to invest," said Frances Cloud, analyst for east Europe at Nomura Equity Research in London.
"But at the same time I think the stocks are quite expensive."
On Tuesday pharmaceuticals Egis and hotel firm Danubius were among the top beneficiaries of investors' appetite, traders said.
Danubius rose five percent or 245 forints to finish at 5,095 forints, while Egis gained two and a half percent or 250 forints to end at 10,300.
OTP Bank put on almost three percent or 95 forints to end at 3,495 forints, while the most actively traded chemicals TVK added 50 forints to finish at 2,090.

Retailer Global surged five percent and reached the 2,100 forint level at which its majority owner Tesco made a buyout offer for holders of Global shares which are planned to be delisted from the Budapest bourse.

The BSE said in a statement after the close of the session that it suspended trading in frozen food maker Goldsun GSUN.BU for the day after a newspaper report which contained information that had not yet gone through the market.
The report said that a tender for the sale or for the operational use of the assets in Goldsun, now under liquidation, was unsuccessful, the BSE said.
